from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Can we reach the bottom faster?",
            "Not by taking a straight path.",
            "Compare straight line and curve.",
            "A secret path hides beneath.",
            "This is the Brachistochrone problem."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Challenge of Descent", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        bead_asset = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bead.svg"
        bead_s = SVGMobject(bead_asset, color=BLUE)
        bead_c = SVGMobject(bead_asset, color=BLUE)
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=24)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=24)
        
        # Paths
        straight_path = Line(start=self.grid["C3"], end=self.grid["D4"], color=GRAY)
        curve_path = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([
                self.grid["C3"][0] + t * (self.grid["D4"][0] - self.grid["C3"][0]),
                self.grid["C3"][1] + (t - t**2) * 1.5,
                0
            ]), 
            t_range=[0, 1], 
            color=GRAY
        )
        
        # Positioning requested by VideoCritic
        self.place_at_grid(bead_s, "C3", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(bead_c, "D4", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "C2", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "D3", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(FadeIn(bead_s), FadeIn(bead_c), Write(label_a), Write(label_b))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000")
        self.play(Create(straight_path))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.play(Create(curve_path))
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(bead_s, straight_path),
            MoveAlongPath(bead_c, curve_path),
            run_time=2
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.play(curve_path.animate.set_stroke(color="#FF00FF", width=6))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Intuition: Energy and Velocity", 
                         ["Energy dictates speed, gravity drives descent.", 
                          "Gaining velocity early is crucial.", 
                          "Curvature helps build speed quickly."])
        
        # Assets (loaded once)
        ramp = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ramp.svg")
        ramp.set_color("#FFD700")
        ball = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ball.svg")
        
        # Formula
        formula = MathTex(r"K", "=", "0.5", r"\cdot", "m", r"\cdot", "v^2", color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'A3', 'B5', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Energy Bar (separate rectangles to avoid updater issues)
        energy_bar_bg = Rectangle(height=0.3, width=3, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.2)
        energy_bar_fill = Rectangle(height=0.3, width=0, color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=0.8)
        energy_bar_fill.align_to(energy_bar_bg, LEFT)
        bar_group = VGroup(energy_bar_bg, energy_bar_fill)
        self.place_at_grid(bar_group, 'C4', scale_factor=0.6)

        # ValueTracker
        velocity_val = ValueTracker(0)
        def update_bar(m):
            w = 3 * (velocity_val.get_value() / 5)
            new_fill = Rectangle(height=0.3, width=max(0.01, w), color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=0.8)
            new_fill.align_to(energy_bar_bg, LEFT)
            m.submobjects[1].become(new_fill)

        bar_group.add_updater(update_bar)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.place_in_area(ramp, 'D5', 'E6', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(ramp), FadeIn(bar_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(ball, 'C3', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(ball))
        self.play(velocity_val.animate.set_value(5), run_time=2)
        self.play(Indicate(formula[6])) 

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(formula), FadeOut(bar_group), FadeOut(ramp), FadeOut(ball))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The solution is a Cycloid.",
            "A point on a rolling circle.",
            "It traces a path of wonder.",
            "Mathematics defines this elegant arc.",
            "Optimal descent meets perfect geometry."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Mathematical Reveal: The Cycloid", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # The solution is a Cycloid.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")
        # Use MathTex with the requested term
        cycloid_eq = MathTex(r"x = r(t - \sin t), y = r(1 - \cos t)", color="#FFFF00")
        # Fix 27: Updated positioning for equation
        self.place_in_area(cycloid_eq, 'A2', 'A6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Write(cycloid_eq))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # A point on a rolling circle.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")
        # Use the asset provided: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/circle.svg
        circle = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/circle.svg")
        # Fix 28: Updated positioning for circle
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        point = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        point.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(circle.get_center() + np.array([0.3, 0, 0])))
        self.add(point)
        self.play(FadeIn(circle))
        self.play(circle.animate.shift(RIGHT * 3), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # It traces a path of wonder.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#3357FF")
        path = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([t - np.sin(t), 1 - np.cos(t), 0]),
            t_range=[0, 2 * PI],
            color="#00FF00"
        )
        self.place_at_grid(path, 'E3', scale_factor=0.4)
        self.play(Create(path), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Mathematics defines this elegant arc.
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF33")
        label = Text("Cycloid Path", font_size=20, color="#FFFF00")
        # Fix 29: Updated positioning for label
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'D4', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Optimal descent meets perfect geometry.
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF33FF")
        moving_dot = Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.08)
        self.add(moving_dot)
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(moving_dot, path), run_time=3)
        # Final cleanup including asset
        self.play(FadeOut(cycloid_eq), FadeOut(circle), FadeOut(point), FadeOut(label), FadeOut(moving_dot), FadeOut(path))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application & Summary", [
            "This birthed the calculus of variations.", 
            "Nature uses paths to optimize time.", 
            "From rollercoasters to diving eagles."
        ])
        
        # Define Assets
        eagle_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/eagle.svg"
        eagle = SVGMobject(eagle_path, color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        
        # Cycloid Path Trajectory
        # Parametric: x = r(t - sin(t)), y = -r(1 - cos(t))
        # Note: We anchor this carefully as requested by VideoCritic
        r = 0.3
        def cycloid(t):
            return np.array([r * (t - np.sin(t)), -r * (1 - np.cos(t)), 0])
        
        path = ParametricFunction(cycloid, t_range=[0, 2*PI], color=YELLOW)
        
        # Group path and eagle
        path_group = VGroup(path, eagle)
        self.place_in_area(path_group, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.add(path)
        self.play(FadeIn(eagle))
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(eagle, path), run_time=3)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(self.lecture), FadeOut(self.title), FadeOut(path), FadeOut(eagle))

outline.topic: The Brachistochrone Problem: The Race of Curves

sections.title: Introduction: The Challenge of Descent
sections.content: Define the problem: Given two points A and B at different heights, what is the shape of the path that allows a particle to travel from A to B in the shortest time under gravity?
sections.example: Visual comparison: A straight line vs. a circular arc vs. a mysterious curve. Ask the audience: Is the shortest distance (straight line) also the fastest?

sections.title: Prerequisite Intuition: Energy and Velocity
sections.content: Briefly explain the Conservation of Energy. As the ball drops, potential energy converts to kinetic energy, increasing speed. The path must gain speed early to win the race.
sections.example: Animation: A ball accelerating down a steep slope versus one moving horizontally. Emphasize that 'getting up to speed' quickly is key to minimizing time.

sections.title: The Mathematical Reveal: The Cycloid
sections.content: Introduce the Brachistochrone curve: the Cycloid. Define it as the path traced by a point on the rim of a circle rolling along a straight line.
sections.example: Animation: A rolling wheel with a glowing LED on its rim, tracing the specific path that connects the starting point to the destination.

sections.title: Verification: Why Cycloid Wins
sections.content: Explain that while the straight line is shortest, the cycloid 'sacrifices' distance to gain massive velocity in the early phase, resulting in a shorter total time.
sections.example: Side-by-side race: A marble on a straight ramp vs. a marble on a cycloid ramp. The cycloid marble consistently wins.

sections.title: Real-World Application & Summary
sections.content: Summarize that this problem birthed the Calculus of Variations. Mention real-world applications in roller coaster design and fluid dynamics.
sections.example: An eagle diving to catch prey: Does it follow a straight line or a path that optimizes speed like a cycloid? Conclusion: Nature often optimizes energy and time.

issues.resolution_note: Fixed formula positioning.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The bar_group and ball overlap significantly, causing visual clutter in the center-right of the frame. issues.resolution_note: Fixed ramp positioning.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The cycloid equation overlaps with the circle's top trajectory, causing visual clutter. Fix: Line 61: self.place_in_area(cycloid_eq, 'A2', 'A6', scale_factor=0.5) (line=61, object=cycloid_eq)

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The circle animation is too low, causing it to exit the viewing area prematurely during the descent. Fix: Line 70: self.place_at_grid(circle, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6) (line=70, object=circle)
issues.resolution_note: Repositioned circle object.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The 'Cycloid Path' label is positioned too low and detached from the actual arc, causing poor proximity. Fix: Line 90: self.place_at_grid(label, 'D4', scale_factor=0.7) (line=90, object=label)
